speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing a psychiatric condition alongside a new movement disorder. To begin our assessment, could you describe the specific movements you are noticing and when they started?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful; the timing of your movement symptoms appearing two months after starting risperidone is significant. Are these involuntary movements occurring only in your face and tongue, or do they also affect your limbs and trunk?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Dystonia is unlikely given the description of restlessness and leg-fidgeting; these are classic signs of Akathisia induced by risperidone. Since I have only used 2 of my 10 questions and the diagnosis is clear based on the history and symptoms, no further questions or tests are required at this time.
